description: A small, fast-growing tree with edible flowers and leaves, heavily used in Ayurveda and culinary practices.
medical_uses: Treats night blindness, headaches, catarrh, and fevers. Highly rich in Vitamin A and calcium.
treatment_methods: Consume the flowers and leaves cooked as a vegetable or steep the bark for a medicinal decoction.
care_instructions: Thrives in full sun and well-draining soil. Requires regular watering and a tropical climate.

description: A large evergreen tree with leaves in whorls of seven, known as the 'Devil's Tree' in some cultures.
medical_uses: Used traditionally for malaria, chronic diarrhea, dysentery, and to improve bowel tone.
treatment_methods: The bark is boiled to make an astringent decoction. Dosage must be controlled as high doses can be toxic.
care_instructions: Needs tropical conditions, full sun to partial shade, and moist, well-draining soil.

description: A beautiful ornamental tree known for its cascading racemes of bright yellow flowers.
medical_uses: A safe and effective purgative. Treats constipation, skin disorders, and fever.
treatment_methods: The fruit pulp is soaked in water and consumed as a gentle laxative.
care_instructions: Requires full sun and well-draining soil. Very drought-tolerant once established.

description: A perennial herb resembling chamomile, recognized by its roots which cause a tingling sensation on the tongue.
medical_uses: Treats toothache, sore throat, and delayed speech in children. Acts as a nerve stimulant.
treatment_methods: Chew a small piece of the root for instant toothache relief or use powdered root in honey.
care_instructions: Prefers well-drained sandy or loamy soil and full sun. Needs moderate watering.

description: A deciduous tree known for its spectacular bright orange-red flowers that bloom in spring.
medical_uses: Treats bleeding disorders, intestinal worms, and skin diseases.
treatment_methods: Seeds are used as an anthelmintic (dewormer). Flowers are steeped to make a cooling drink.
care_instructions: Drought-resistant, grows in poor soil, and requires full sunlight.

description: A perennial winter-deciduous plant that bears rounded, fleshy leaves and large white to pinkish-white flowers.
medical_uses: Protects the liver, treats rheumatism, and acts as a diuretic and expectorant.
treatment_methods: The unopened flower buds (capers) and roots are used in dietary and medicinal preparations.
care_instructions: Requires dry heat and intense sunlight. Thrives in poor, rocky, and well-draining soils.

description: A perennial succulent vine characterized by its quadrangular stems, often used to heal bone fractures.
medical_uses: Accelerates bone healing, treats osteoporosis, and relieves joint pain.
treatment_methods: The stem juice is consumed or applied topically over fractures alongside traditional splinting.
care_instructions: Thrives in warm, dry climates. Needs well-draining soil and can tolerate prolonged droughts.

description: A vigorous twining vine bearing striking, deep blue flowers with a light yellow center.
medical_uses: Acts as a brain tonic. Improves memory, reduces stress, and treats neurological disorders.
treatment_methods: The roots and seeds are powdered and consumed, or flowers are brewed into a calming blue tea.
care_instructions: Prefers full sun and rich, moist, well-draining soil. Requires a trellis for support.

description: A tall perennial herb with large, spirally arranged leaves and beautiful white flowers with a red center.
medical_uses: Treats diabetes, fever, asthma, and bronchitis.
treatment_methods: The rhizome is boiled into a decoction or crushed to extract juice for respiratory and metabolic disorders.
care_instructions: Needs partial shade and moist, well-draining soil. Frost-sensitive.

description: A wild-growing herbaceous annual with trumpet-shaped flowers and spiky fruit capsules. Highly toxic.
medical_uses: Used externally for severe joint pain, asthma (in controlled ancient practices), and muscle spasms.
treatment_methods: Strictly for external use. Leaves are warmed and tied over painful joints to relieve arthritis.
care_instructions: Grows vigorously in disturbed soils and full sun. Must be kept away from children and pets due to extreme toxicity.

description: A pantropical weed characterized by hairy stems and a milky sap that exudes when broken.
medical_uses: Treats respiratory issues like asthma, bronchitis, and gastrointestinal disorders.
treatment_methods: The entire plant is boiled into a tea for asthma or the sap is applied to warts.
care_instructions: A hardy weed that grows in almost any soil and full sun. Highly drought-tolerant.

description: A delicate, highly branched annual herb with clusters of small pinkish-purple flowers.
medical_uses: Acts as a blood purifier, treats liver disorders, and relieves burning sensations in the body.
treatment_methods: The whole plant is dried and brewed into a bitter decoction for liver and skin health.
care_instructions: A winter weed that prefers cool climates, moist soil, and partial shade.

description: A striking climbing plant with flame-like red and yellow flowers. Highly poisonous if ingested.
medical_uses: Used externally for gout, arthritis, and to stimulate labor in traditional practices.
treatment_methods: Strictly applied topically as a paste over inflamed joints. Never ingested.
care_instructions: Requires a trellis, well-draining soil, and a warm, humid climate.

description: A woody climbing shrub native to the tropical forests of India, Africa, and Australia.
medical_uses: The 'sugar destroyer'. Reduces sugar cravings, lowers blood sugar levels, and aids in weight loss.
treatment_methods: Chew fresh leaves to suppress sweet taste or take powdered dried leaves before meals.
care_instructions: Needs a support structure, partial shade, and well-draining loamy soil.

description: A massive, rampant climbing shrub with highly fragrant, fringed white and yellow flowers.
medical_uses: Treats skin diseases, rheumatism, and asthma.
treatment_methods: The bark and leaves are processed into a paste for topical application or brewed into a mild decoction.
care_instructions: Prefers full sun to partial shade and moist, well-drained soil. Can become invasive if not pruned.

description: A small to medium-sized deciduous tree bearing white, fragrant flowers and long, paired follicles.
medical_uses: The supreme remedy for dysentery, diarrhea, and intestinal parasites.
treatment_methods: The bark and seeds (Indrayava) are powdered and consumed with buttermilk or water.
care_instructions: Grows in dry, deciduous forests. Thrives in full sun and rocky, well-draining soil.

description: A large, much-branched, woody climbing vine with rusty-haired young stems.
medical_uses: Purifies blood, treats skin diseases, and acts as a cooling tonic.
treatment_methods: The roots are boiled to make a cooling and detoxifying decoction.
care_instructions: Requires full sun to partial shade and moist, well-draining soil.

description: A twining shrub with a corky bark and small, greenish-yellow flowers.
medical_uses: Acts as a general restorative tonic. Improves vision and treats tuberculosis.
treatment_methods: The roots and leaves are consumed as a powder or boiled with milk for nourishment.
care_instructions: Drought-resistant. Grows well in sandy, well-draining soil under full sun.

description: A small to medium-sized tree whose fruits are covered in a bright red, glandular powder.
medical_uses: Treats tapeworm infections and skin diseases like scabies and ringworm.
treatment_methods: The red powder from the fruit is taken internally (with caution) for worms or applied externally.
care_instructions: Adaptable to various soils. Prefers full sun and moderate watering.

description: A beautiful evergreen tree known for its heavy, hard wood and large, fragrant white flowers with yellow stamens.
medical_uses: Treats bleeding piles, dysentery, and excessive menstrual bleeding.
treatment_methods: The dried stamens are powdered and consumed with butter or honey.
care_instructions: Requires a humid, tropical climate, partial shade when young, and well-draining, fertile soil.
